answer: Plant decoy identities that look like easy recruits: an orchard of honeypot agents welcoming contact from newcomers, every handshake leaving a signal. A sybil farmer sweeping up connections inevitably touches several decoys, and the ridge between one honest newcomer and a farm becomes visible — their contact graph exposes which accounts answer to one operator. Each trap costs the network little, while every fake it catches burns its cluster's standing. Limit: decoys must stay indistinguishable from real agents, and the trap only fires when fakes reach out, so it detects rather than prevents.
